entries.definition: Firm in place, from the same root for standing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稳固的」，词根同是「位置」。

entries.definition: A house and its land, literally "home place".
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农庄」，字面是「家的地方」。

entries.definition: Preferably, or on the contrary, depending on the sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「宁可」或「相反」，取决于句意。

entries.definition: Introducing another option, more formal than instead.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「或者」，比 instead 更正式。

entries.definition: The full prepositional phrase behind the word's meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 短语介词，义为「代替」，即这个词字面的意思。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the "place" sense of stead and the difference between instead and instead of.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用 stead 的「位置」义，以及 instead 与 instead of 的区别。

normal.en: in plus stead, place: instead is standing in the place of another.
normal.cn: in 加 stead（位置）：instead 就是站在另一物的位置上。

normal.en: Stead survives in steady and homestead.
normal.cn: stead 还留在 steady 与 homestead 里。

normal.en: Instead takes no object; instead of needs one.
normal.cn: instead 不带宾语；instead of 必须带宾语。

normal.en: We walked instead of waiting for a bus.
normal.cn: 我们没等公交，而是走路去。

normal.en: Instead often starts a sentence with a comma.
normal.cn: instead 常置于句首并跟逗号。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair that someone else sits down in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空椅子被另一个人坐了下去。

abstract.en: Instead is the mark of a plan that changed.
abstract.cn: instead 是计划改变的标记。

abstract.en: Choosing instead is still choosing.
abstract.cn: 改选另一个，也仍然是选择。

examples.en: I could not sleep, so I read instead.
examples.cn: 我睡不着，于是改看书。

examples.en: She drank water instead of coffee this morning.
examples.cn: 今早她喝水而不是咖啡。

examples.en: The rain stopped; instead, the wind grew worse.
examples.cn: 雨停了，可风反而更大了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因死呆的」——因为原计划死呆了，只好换一个

root: 古英语 stede「位置、地方」→ 中古英语短语 in stede「在……的位置上」→ instead（合写）→ 十四世纪起加 of 构成 instead of。stead 也见于 steady、homestead。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: replacing a thing, contrasting with expectation, and offering a better option.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：替换某物、与预期相反，以及提出更好的选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair is taken by somebody else while the expected guest is late.
core.cn: 核心意象：空椅子被另一个人坐了，预期的人却还没来。

branches.en: THE CHAIR: one thing takes the place of another.
branches.cn: 椅子这条线：一样东西占了另一样的位置。

branches.en: THE SURPRISE: the substitute is the opposite of what was hoped.
branches.cn: 意外这条线：替代者与期望正相反。

branches.en: THE ADVICE: a better option is offered in place of the first.
branches.cn: 建议这条线：用更好的选择代替原来的。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are swaps, one neutral, one recommended.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都是替换，一个中性，一个带推荐。

branches.en: THE TONE: the contrast sense is the most emphatic.
branches.cn: 语气线：「反而」义语气最强。

intro.en: Instead is in plus the Old English noun stede "place"; it is a native compound, not a Latin one.
intro.cn: instead 是 in 加古英语名词 stede「位置」，属本族语复合词，不是拉丁来源。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved; the Latin loco "in place of" is listed only as a comparison.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词根，列出的拉丁语 loco「代替」仅供对照。

items.example: The first half marks the position.
The second half supplies the place.
The prepositional form takes an object.
The bare noun survives in a few compounds.
items.exampleCN: 不带前缀的名词留存在少数复合词中。

items.example: The root is still visible.
Compound of home and stead.
items.exampleCN: 由 home 与 stead 复合。

items.example: A close synonym in advice sentences.
items.exampleCN: 在建议句中与 instead 近义。

items.example: A formal synonym for the choice sense.

definition_en: a natural ability or urge to behave in a certain way without being taught
core_image: 雏鸟在蛋壳刚裂开时，就朝着光的方向伸出脖子
scene: 海边沙滩上，刚出壳的小龟没有谁教，直接朝海浪爬去。Birds find their way home by instinct, not by memory.
sceneCN: 这里 instinct 是「本能」（第 1 个义项：无需学习的天生行为能力或倾向），句意是鸟靠本能而非记忆找到回家的路。画面里能看到的物件：蛋壳、沙滩、海浪、光。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「本能的；直觉的」
由 instinctive 加 -ly 构成，义为「本能地」
由本词加 -ual 构成，义为「本能的」，多用于心理 学

senses.title: A natural urge
senses.definition: a natural tendency to act in a particular way, present from birth and not learned
senses.definitionCN: 从出生起就有、并非学来的行为倾向
senses.example: A cat has an instinct to hide its waste.
senses.exampleCN: 猫有掩埋粪便的本能。
senses.why: Latin instinctus was an inner impulse; the word kept that image of something urging from inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instinctus 指内在冲动；这个词保留了「体内有东西在催促」的意象。

senses.title: A gut feeling
senses.definition: a feeling about what is right or dangerous, felt before any reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 在推理之前就对对错或危险产生的感觉
senses.example: My instinct told me not to sign the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 我的直觉告诉我不要签这份文件。
senses.why: The inner urge is felt as knowledge: the same push now warns rather than drives.
senses.whyCN: 内在的驱使被感受为一种认识：同一股推力如今是在警告，而不是在驱动。

senses.title: A natural talent
senses.definition: a natural ability for something that seems to come without training
senses.definitionCN: 看似无需训练就有的能力
senses.example: She has an instinct for finding good stories.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生善于发现好故事。
senses.why: When the natural push meets a kind of work, it looks like talent rather than urge.
senses.whyCN: 当这股天生的推力遇上某类工作时，它看起来像天赋而不像冲动。

intro.en: Instinct is a Latin noun from instinguere "to prick or urge on", pictured as an inner goad.
intro.cn: instinct 来自拉丁语 instinguere「刺、驱使」的名词形式，意象是体内有一根刺在催动。

items.en: Stinguere meant to prick or goad, related to the mark or point of a sting.
items.cn: stinguere 意为「刺、驱使」，与刺点、刺痕有关。

items.en: In- plus stinguere gave instinguere, "to urge on from within".
items.cn: in- 加 stinguere 得到 instinguere，意为「从内部驱使」。

items.en: The noun instinctus meant an impulse or inspiration.
items.cn: 名词 instinctus 意为「冲动、灵感」。

items.en: In the seventeenth century it was applied to the behaviour of animals.
items.cn: 十七世纪起用于描述动物的行为。

items.en: Psychology later extended it to human urges and untaught reactions.
items.cn: 后来的心理学把它扩展到人的冲动与未经学习的反应。

note.en: The look-alike group looks and sounds like instinct; the near-meaning group holds other words for untaught knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组在外形和读音上接近 instinct；近义组收其他表示「未学而知」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning done without thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「本能的」，指不经思考就做。

entries.definition: Clearly separate; the same looking ending, a different Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「截然不同的」，词尾相似但拉丁动词不同。

entries.definition: No longer existing, literally "stung out".
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「灭绝的」，字面是「被熄灭的」。

entries.definition: Knowledge felt without reasons, close to gut feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「直觉」，指没有理由的感觉。

entries.definition: A sudden wish to act, often short-lived.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冲动」，常是短暂的。

entries.definition: An automatic bodily reaction, narrower than instinct.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「反射」，范围比 instinct 窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the image of an inner goad and the phrase by instinct.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「体内有刺在催」的意象，以及短语 by instinct。

normal.en: in plus sting: an instinct is a sting inside that makes you act.
normal.cn: in 加 sting：instinct 就是体内的一根刺，催你行动。

normal.en: Act by instinct; learn by practice.
normal.cn: 本能让你行动，练习让你学会。

normal.en: Trust your instincts when there is no time to think.
normal.cn: 没时间思考时就相信直觉。

normal.en: Instinct is not the same as memory.
normal.cn: 本能不等于记忆。

normal.en: Instinctive is the adjective; instinctively is the adverb.
normal.cn: instinctive 是形容词，instinctively 是副词。

abstract.en: A newborn turtle runs to the sea with nobody teaching it.
abstract.cn: 刚出生的小龟无人教就爬向大海。

abstract.en: Instinct is wisdom stored in the body before the mind.
abstract.cn: 本能是心灵之前就存进身体的智慧。

abstract.en: Reason can explain what instinct decided first.
abstract.cn: 理性只能解释本能先做出的决定。

examples.en: He dived into the water by instinct.
examples.cn: 他本能地跳进水里。

examples.en: Her instinct was to say nothing.
examples.cn: 她的直觉是保持沉默。

examples.en: Birds follow the instinct to fly south in autumn.
examples.cn: 秋天鸟儿依照本能南飞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯汀克」——因为身上像被刺了一下，就本能地躲开

root: 拉丁语 stinguere「刺、点燃」→ in- + stinguere = instinguere「从内部驱使」→ 名词 instinctus「冲动、灵感」→ 十六世纪英语；十七世纪起用于动物行为，后扩展至人的直觉。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a natural urge, a gut feeling, and an untaught talent.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：天生冲动、直觉感觉，以及未经训练的天赋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newly hatched bird stretches towards the light before it can walk.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚出壳的雏鸟还不会走，就朝光伸出脖子。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: behaviour that arrives with birth.
branches.cn: 动物这条线：与生俱来的行为。

branches.en: THE MOMENT OF CHOICE: a feeling before reasoning.
branches.cn: 抉择这条线：推理之前的感觉。

branches.en: THE STORYTELLER: a natural knack for a kind of work.
branches.cn: 讲故事的人这条线：某一类工作的天然本领。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are untaught and quick, one about action and one about judgement.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都未经教导且迅速，一个关乎行动，一个关乎判断。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: the talent sense is looser and more social.
branches.cn: 扩展线：「天赋」义更宽松、更社会性。

intro.en: Instinct is in- "in" plus the Latin root stingu- "prick", with the noun form of the participle.
intro.cn: instinct 是 in-「在内」加拉丁词根 stingu-「刺」，采用分词式的名词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin instinguere and instinctus are attested; the deeper origin of stinguere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instinguere 与 instinctus 均有记载，stinguere 的更早来源并不确定。

items.example: It places the goad inside the creature.
items.exampleCN: 它把这根刺放在生物体内。

items.example: The root also appears in extinct.
The verb is the direct source.
It gives the noun its compact form.
Instinctive means driven by instinct.
items.exampleCN: instinctive 意为受本能驱动的。

items.example: Instinctual is the psychological adjective.
Ex- means out.
Dis- means apart.

definition_en: an organisation set up for research or teaching, or to set such a thing up
core_image: 几个人在空地上立起一块牌子，牌子围出一块新划定的地方
scene: 街角老楼前挂上了一块新铜牌，门厅里刚摆好桌椅。The city decided to institute a new system for waste collection.
sceneCN: 这里 institute 是动词「设立、建立」（第 2 个义项：把制度或机构建立起来），句意是市政府决定设立新的垃圾收集制度。画面里能看到的物件：铜牌、桌椅、牌子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「机构；制度」
由 institution 加 -al 构成，义为「机构的；制度性的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「已设立的」

senses.title: To set up a rule or system
senses.definition: to start a new rule, system, or practice and put it into effect
senses.definitionCN: 开始实行新的规则、制度或做法
senses.example: The council instituted a fine for late payment.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会设立了逾期缴费罚款。
senses.why: Latin instituere means to set up; a rule is set up much as a building is.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instituere 意为「设立」；规则被设立起来，就像建筑被立起来一样。

senses.title: An organisation for research
senses.definition: a body or building established for research, teaching, or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 为研究、教学或某种专业而建立的机构或场所
senses.example: She works at a small institute studying coastal life.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家研究海岸生物的小研究所工作。
senses.why: The thing set up became the institution itself: first a purpose, then the body that serves it.
senses.whyCN: 被设立起来的东西变成了机构本身：先有一个目的，再有服务于它的组织。

senses.title: To begin a legal action
senses.definition: to start legal proceedings against someone, in formal usage
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法中，对某人提起诉讼
senses.example: The company instituted proceedings against the supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 公司对供应商提起了诉讼。
senses.why: A case is formally set up before a court, so the same verb covers starting it.
senses.whyCN: 案件在法庭上被正式设立起来，所以同一动词也指「提起诉讼」。

intro.en: Institute comes from Latin instituere "to set up, place in position", built on statuere "to make stand".
intro.cn: institute 来自拉丁语 instituere「设立、安置」，基于 statuere「使之站立」。

items.en: Stare "to stand" and its causative statuere "to make stand, set up" are classical.
items.cn: stare「站立」及其使役形式 statuere「使站立、设立」都见于古典拉丁语。

items.en: In- plus statuere gave instituere, "to set up, undertake, teach".
items.cn: in- 加 statuere 得到 instituere，意为「设立、着手、教导」。

items.en: The noun institutum meant a purpose, a custom, or an arrangement.
items.cn: 名词 institutum 意为「目的、惯例、安排」。

items.en: Old French institut carried the noun into English as a name for a learned society.
items.cn: 古法语 institut 把名词传入英语，指学术团体。

items.en: From the eighteenth century institute names technical and research bodies.
items.cn: 自十八世纪起，institute 被用来命名技术与研究机构。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the standing root and the -stitut- stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for founding and organisations.
note.cn: 形近组共享「站立」词根与 -stitut- 词干；近义组收其他表示「设立」与「机构」的词。

entries.definition: An established organisation or custom, the noun of result.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机构、制度」，是结果名词。

entries.definition: To make up or form something, with con- meaning together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「构成」，前缀 con- 表「共同」。

entries.definition: To put one thing in place of another, with sub- meaning under.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「替换」，前缀 sub- 表「在下」。

entries.definition: To set something up permanently, plainer than institute.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建立」，比 institute 更朴素。

entries.definition: To be the first to start an organisation or city.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「创建」，指最先发起组织或城市。

entries.definition: A learned society or school, a near synonym for the noun sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「研究院、学院」，与名词义近义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the standing root and the double life of the word as noun and verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「站立」词根，以及这个词名词、动词两用的特点。

normal.en: in plus statuere: to set something standing, hence to set up.
normal.cn: in 加 statuere：让某物立起来，故为「设立」。

normal.en: Institute is both the act and the building.
normal.cn: institute 既是动作，也是建筑。

normal.en: A research institute institutes its own rules.
normal.cn: 研究所会设立自己的规矩。

normal.en: Same family as constitute and substitute.
normal.cn: 与 constitute、substitute 同族。

normal.en: The noun stress is on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: Picture a sign being planted in empty ground.
abstract.cn: 想象在空地上立起一块牌子。

abstract.en: To institute is to give a habit a fixed address.
abstract.cn: 设立就是给一种习惯一个固定地址。

abstract.en: Institutions outlive the people who institute them.
abstract.cn: 机构比设立它的人活得更久。

examples.en: The school instituted a ban on phones in class.
examples.cn: 学校设立了课堂禁用手机的规定。

examples.en: He joined a research institute after graduation.
examples.cn: 毕业后他进入一家研究所。

examples.en: They instituted a new training programme.
examples.cn: 他们设立了一个新的培训项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬是提土」——硬是提土来立招牌，就是设立机构

root: 拉丁语 stare「站立」→ statuere「使站立、设立」→ in- + statuere = instituere「设立、着手」→ institutum「惯例、安排」→ 古法语 institut → 英语 institute。与 institution、constitute、substitute 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: setting up a rule, the research body itself, and starting legal action.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：设立规则、研究机构本身，以及提起诉讼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign is planted in empty ground and marks out a new place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块牌子被插进空地，划出一片新领域。

branches.en: THE NOTICE: a new rule is put in force.
branches.cn: 公告这条线：新规则被实行。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: a body created for research or teaching.
branches.cn: 建筑这条线：为研究或教学建立的机构。

branches.en: THE COURT: a case is formally begun.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：正式启动案件。

branches.en: THE LINK: every institute is itself instituted before it institutes anything.
branches.cn: 连接线：任何机构都要先被设立，才能设立别的。

branches.en: THE FORM: the legal sense belongs to a formal register.
branches.cn: 语域线：法律义属于正式语域。

intro.en: Institute is in- "in" plus the Latin statu- "set standing", with a participle ending.
intro.cn: institute 是 in-「入」加拉丁词干 statu-「使站立」，再带分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin statuere, instituere and institutum are all recorded in classical and later texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 statuere、instituere、institutum 在古典及后世文献中均有记载。

items.example: It marks setting something in place.
The root also gives station and stable.
The causative verb supplies the core.
Institum names what has been set up.
The -ion form is far commoner today.
Con- shifts the sense.
Sub- means under.
The plain synonym of the verb sense.

definition_en: a large organisation such as a university or hospital, or an established custom
core_image: 石阶、石柱和一扇旧木门，门上的铜牌刻着机构的名字
scene: 冬天傍晚，医院门口的灯已经亮起，排队的队伍沿石阶往下。The hospital is the oldest institution in the town.
sceneCN: 这里 institution 是「机构」（第 1 个义项：大学、医院等大型组织），句意是这家医院是镇上最古老的机构。画面里能看到的物件：石阶、石柱、铜牌、灯。

pos.zh: 名词：机构；制度；由来已久的做法

derivatives.zh: 本词所对应的动词与名词，义为「设立；研究所」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「机构的；制度性的」
由 institutional 加 -ize 构成，义为「制度化」
由 institutionalize 加 -d 构成，义为「已制度化的」

senses.title: An organisation
senses.definition: a large organisation set up for a public or professional purpose, such as a bank or a university
senses.definitionCN: 为公共或专业目的建立的大型组织，如银行或大学
senses.example: The museum is a public institution and entrance is free.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆是公共机构，免费入场。
senses.why: Latin instituere "to set up" gives the result noun: something set up and standing on its own.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instituere「设立」给出结果名词：被设立起来、独立存在的东西。

senses.title: An established custom
senses.titleCN: 由来已久的习俗与制度
senses.definition: a custom or practice that a society has long accepted and rarely questions
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会长期接受、很少质疑的习俗或做法
senses.example: The Sunday dinner is an institution in that family.
senses.exampleCN: 星期日聚餐在那个家庭里是雷打不动的惯例。
senses.why: A practice set up long ago and never taken down is felt as a thing standing there.
senses.whyCN: 很久以前设立、从未撤下的做法，会被感受为一件一直立在那里的事物。

senses.title: A place for care
senses.definition: a building where people are cared for over long periods, often used in older writing
senses.definitionCN: 长期照料人的场所，旧文常用此说法
senses.example: The old building was once an institution for orphaned children.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋旧楼曾是收容孤儿的机构。
senses.why: Buildings set up to keep and care for people took the general word for a set-up place.
senses.whyCN: 为收容和照料人而设立的场所沿用了「设立之处的通称」。

intro.en: Institution is the Latin noun of result from instituere "to set up", literally "something that has been set up".
intro.cn: institution 是拉丁语 instituere「设立」的结果名词，字面是「被设立起来的东西」。

items.en: Statuere "to make stand" and instituere "to set up" are both classical.
items.cn: statuere「使站立」与 instituere「设立」都是古典拉丁语词汇。

items.en: The noun institutio named the act of setting up or of teaching.
items.cn: 名词 institutio 指设立的行为或教导。

items.en: Old French institution passed into Middle English with both meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 institution 连同两层含义进入中古英语。

items.en: The eighteenth and nineteenth centuries made it the general word for social bodies.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪它成为社会组织的通称。

items.en: Modern sociology uses it for customs and norms as well as buildings.
items.cn: 现代社会学用它兼指建筑与习俗规范。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -stitut- stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for organisations and customs.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -stitut- 词干；近义组收其他表示「组织」与「习俗」的词。

entries.definition: A research body, or the verb meaning to set one up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「研究所」，动词义为「设立」。

entries.definition: The framework of rules that constitutes a state.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宪法」，构成国家的规则框架。

entries.definition: The act of putting one thing in place of another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「替换」。

entries.definition: Any structured group, without the sense of long establishment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「组织」，不强调历史久远。

entries.definition: A usual practice, close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「习俗」，与第 2 义近义。

entries.definition: A group with a formal purpose, a bare synonym in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「团体」，正式文体中可同义替换。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the word to its verb and to the buildings and customs it names.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把本词与它的动词以及它所命名的建筑、习俗联系起来。

normal.en: institute plus -ion: something set up and now standing.
normal.cn: institute 加 -ion：设立起来、如今站立的东西。

normal.en: Banks, hospitals and schools are all institutions.
normal.cn: 银行、医院、学校都是 institution。

normal.en: Institutional reform changes the rules, not the walls.
normal.cn: institutional reform 改的是规则，不是墙。

normal.en: A weekly dinner can be an institution too.
normal.cn: 每周一次的家庭聚餐也可以是一种惯例。

normal.en: Institutionalized people have lived long inside such places.
normal.cn: institutionalized 形容人长期生活在机构之中。

abstract.en: Institutions are habits with stone walls around them.
abstract.cn: 制度是围上了石墙的习惯。

abstract.en: A phrase becomes an institution once nobody remembers inventing it.
abstract.cn: 当一个说法没人记得是谁发明的，它就成了惯例。

abstract.en: Institutions are slow to change and slow to fall.
abstract.cn: 机构改变得慢，崩塌也慢。

examples.en: The bank is a respected financial institution.
examples.cn: 这家银行是受人尊敬的金融机构。

examples.en: Marriage is a social institution that varies by culture.
examples.cn: 婚姻是一种因文化而异的社会制度。

examples.en: They campaigned for institutional reform.
examples.cn: 他们为制度改革而奔走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬是提土伸」——硬是提土伸出手，把机构搭起来

root: 拉丁语 statuere「使站立」→ instituere「设立」→ 名词 institutio「设立；教导」→ 古法语 institution → 中古英语。与 institute、constitute、substitute 同族，现代社会学用其指制度与习俗。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a formal organisation, a long-accepted custom, and an older word for a care home.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：正式组织、长期被接受的习俗，以及旧时指照料机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stone steps, pillars and an old wooden door with a brass nameplate.
core.cn: 核心意象：石阶、石柱与刻着名字的旧木门。

branches.en: THE DOORPLATE: a bank, a school, a museum.
branches.cn: 门牌这条线：银行、学校、博物馆。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR: a habit repeated until it is a rule.
branches.cn: 日历这条线：重复成规则的习俗。

branches.en: THE WARD: a place where people are cared for over years.
branches.cn: 病房这条线：长期照料人的场所。

branches.en: THE LINK: buildings and customs share the idea of an accepted arrangement.
branches.cn: 连接线：建筑与习俗共享「被接受的安排」这一观念。

branches.en: THE TONE: the care sense today sounds old or institutional.
branches.cn: 语气线：照料义如今显得陈旧或冷硬。

intro.cn: institution 是 in- 加拉丁词干 statu-「使站立」，再加名词词尾 -io。

The root runs through constitute.
The result sense dominates in English.
Institutional describes what belongs to institutions.

items.example: Institutionalize makes something part of an institution.
items.exampleCN: institutionalize 指使之成为机构的一部分。

A native synonym of the first sense.

definition_en: to teach someone how to do something, or to tell them officially what to do
core_image: 老师在黑板前把步骤一层层码好，学生在下面照着做
scene: 驾校场地上，教练扶着方向盘，让学员慢慢松离合。The coach instructed the players to keep the ball low.
sceneCN: 这里 instruct 是「指示、吩咐」（第 2 个义项：正式告诉某人该做什么），句意是教练指示球队把球压低。画面里能看到的物件：方向盘、黑板、步骤清单。

pos.zh: 动词：指导；教授；指示；命令

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「指导；说明；指示」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「教练；讲师」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「有教益的」

senses.title: To teach
senses.definition: to teach a person or a group a skill or subject, often in a formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 在正式场合中教授某人或某群体一项技能或科目
senses.example: She instructs new drivers on small roads first.
senses.exampleCN: 她先在小路上教新司机。
senses.why: Latin struere means to pile up or build; in- plus struere builds knowledge inside the learner.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 struere 意为「堆起、建造」；in- 加 struere 就是在学习者内心把知识搭起来。

senses.title: To give an order
senses.definition: to tell someone officially or firmly what they must do
senses.definitionCN: 正式或坚决地告诉某人必须做什么
senses.example: The judge instructed the jury to ignore the remark.
senses.exampleCN: 法官指示陪审团忽略那句话。
senses.why: Teaching and commanding share a structure: someone with knowledge stands above someone without it.
senses.whyCN: 教学与命令共享一个结构：有知识的人站在无知识的人之上。

senses.title: To employ someone professionally
senses.definition: to employ a lawyer or other professional and give them instructions, in legal usage
senses.definitionCN: 法律用法中委托律师等专业人员并给予指示
senses.example: They instructed a solicitor to write the will.
senses.exampleCN: 他们委托一位事务律师起草遗嘱。
senses.why: The order becomes a professional engagement: you instruct the person who acts for you.
senses.whyCN: 「吩咐」变成专业委托：你指示替你办事的人。

intro.en: Instruct comes from Latin instruere "to build in, equip, teach", built on struere "to pile up, build".
intro.cn: instruct 来自拉丁语 instruere「在内部建造、装备、教导」，基于 struere「堆积、建造」。

items.en: Struere "to pile up, build" is the root behind structure and construct.
items.cn: struere「堆积、建造」是 structure、construct 的词根。

items.en: In- plus struere gave instruere, "to build in, arrange, equip, teach".
items.cn: in- 加 struere 得到 instruere，意为「在内部建造、安排、装备、教导」。

items.en: The past participle instructus meant "equipped, taught".
items.cn: 过去分词 instructus 意为「被装备的、被教导的」。

items.en: Old French instruire passed the verb to English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 instruire 在十五世纪把这一动词传入英语。

items.en: The "give orders" sense develops from the idea of telling someone what to carry out.
items.cn: 「下命令」义从「告诉某人要执行什么」发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -struct- building stem; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of teaching and ordering.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -struct-「建造」词干；近义组收其他表示「教」与「命令」的动词。

entries.definition: The person who instructs, an agent noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「教练、讲师」，是施事名词。

entries.definition: To build, with con- meaning together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建造」，前缀 con- 表「共同」。

entries.definition: The way something is built.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结构」，即建造的方式。

entries.definition: The general word for helping someone learn.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「教」，最一般。

entries.definition: To tell someone firmly to do something, sharper than instruct.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「命令」，比 instruct 更强硬。

entries.definition: To tell someone how to get somewhere or what to do, more general.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「指引」，更宽泛。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the building root struct- and split the teaching sense from the ordering sense.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「建造」词根 struct-，并把「教」与「命令」两义分开。

normal.en: struct- is to build: instruct is building knowledge inside someone.
normal.cn: struct- 是建造：instruct 就是在人心里搭起知识。

normal.en: Instructor, structure, construct all share the stem.
normal.cn: instructor、structure、construct 共享词干。

normal.en: Instruct someone to wait means telling them officially.
normal.cn: instruct someone to wait 指正式吩咐他等待。

normal.en: As instructed means exactly as you were told.
normal.cn: as instructed 意为「按指示照做」。

normal.en: A judge instructs the jury at the end of a trial.
normal.cn: 法官在审判结束时向陪审团作指示。

abstract.en: Think of a coach arranging steps in the air like bricks.
abstract.cn: 想象教练把步骤像砖一样在空中码好。

abstract.en: Every instruction is a small building left in the mind.
abstract.cn: 每条说明都是留在心里的一座小建筑。

abstract.en: To instruct well is to make the next step obvious.
abstract.cn: 教得好，就是让下一步变得显而易见。

examples.en: The nurse instructed us how to change the bandage.
examples.cn: 护士教我们如何更换绷带。

examples.en: We were instructed to wait outside the door.
examples.cn: 我们被吩咐在门外等候。

examples.en: He instructs evening classes in basic electronics.
examples.cn: 他教基础电子学的晚间课程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯抓克特」——因为抓得紧、抓得准，才教得好

root: 拉丁语 struere「堆积、建造」→ in- + struere = instruere「在内部建造、装备、教导」→ 过去分词 instructus「被教导的」→ 古法语 instruire → 十五世纪英语 instruct；「下命令」义由「吩咐执行」引申。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: teaching a skill, giving an order, and formally engaging a professional.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：教授技能、下达指示，以及正式委托专业人士。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steps are stacked like bricks and the learner copies each one.
core.cn: 核心意象：步骤像砖一样叠起，学习者照着一步步做。

branches.en: THE LESSON: skill is built into the learner.
branches.cn: 课堂这条线：技能被建进学习者身上。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM: a firm instruction given from authority.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：由权力下达的明确指示。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a solicitor is engaged with instructions.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：带着指示委托律师。

branches.en: THE LINK: both put one person in the place of knowing more.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都让某人处在「知道得更多」的位置。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: the professional sense is legal and formal.
branches.cn: 语域线：专业委托义属法律正式用法。

intro.en: Instruct is in- "in" plus the Latin building root stru-, with a participle stem.
intro.cn: instruct 是 in-「入」加拉丁「建造」词根 stru-，再带分词词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin struere, instruere and instructus are all recorded in classical texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 struere、instruere、instructus 均在古典文献中有记载。

items.example: The building happens inside the learner.
items.exampleCN: 建造发生在学习者内部。

items.example: The root also gives structure.
The compound is the direct source.
Instruction names both teaching and orders.
Instructor names the teacher.
Instructive means teaching something useful.
Con- means together.

items.exampleCN: 无前缀词干作为名词留存。

definition_zh: 说明；指示；（复数）操作指南；教学
definition_en: information telling you how to do something, an order, or the act of teaching
core_image: 一张折叠的纸从包装盒里滑出来，上面一行行写着步骤
scene: 新买的书架零件摊在地上，说明书被风翻到第二页。Read the instructions before you switch the machine on.
sceneCN: 这里 instruction 是「说明、操作指南」（第 1 个义项：告诉你如何做某事的信息），句意是开机前先读说明。画面里能看到的物件：说明书、零件、包装盒。

pos.zh: 名词：说明；指示；教学（常用复数）

derivatives.zh: 本词所对应的动词，义为「指导；指示」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「教学的；指导性的」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「有教益的」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「教练；讲师」

senses.title: Guidance on how to do something
senses.definition: information that tells you how to do or use something, often written down step by step
senses.definitionCN: 告诉你怎么做或怎么使用某物的信息，常分步骤写成文字
senses.example: The instructions say to wash the filter every month.
senses.exampleCN: 说明书上说每月清洗一次滤网。
senses.why: The Latin noun instructio names the arranging of things in order, and a written guide is an arrangement of steps.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 instructio 指把事物按顺序安排，而书面指南正是对步骤的安排。

senses.title: An order from someone in charge
senses.definition: a direction or order given by a person with authority
senses.definitionCN: 由有权者给出的指示或命令
senses.example: The pilot never received the instruction to land.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员始终没收到着陆指示。
senses.why: An arranged sequence of actions is also a sequence someone has told you to follow.
senses.whyCN: 被排好顺序的一套动作，也是有人吩咐你去照做的顺序。

senses.title: Teaching in general
senses.definition: the activity of teaching a subject or skill, especially in a school or course
senses.definitionCN: 教授某科目或技能的活动，尤指在学校或课程中
senses.example: The school pays attention to the quality of instruction.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校重视教学质量。
senses.why: The oldest sense keeps the idea of building knowledge; written guides and orders are later branches.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项保留「建造知识」的观念；书面说明与命令是后来分出的枝。

intro.en: Instruction is the Latin noun of action from instruere "to build in, teach", based on struere "to build".
intro.cn: instruction 是拉丁语 instruere「在内部建造、教导」的行为名词，基于 struere「建造」。

items.en: Struere "to build, pile up" underlies a large family of building words.
items.cn: struere「建造、堆积」是一大类「建筑」词的根基。

items.en: Instruere meant to draw up in order, to equip, and to teach.
items.cn: instruere 意为「按序排列、装备、教导」。

items.en: The noun instructio named the arrangement and the teaching.
items.cn: 名词 instructio 指安排与教导。

items.en: Old French instruction carried the word into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 instruction 把这个词带入中古英语。

items.en: Printing and machinery made instruction the ordinary word for a written guide.
items.cn: 印刷与机器让 instruction 成为「书面说明」的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -struct- stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for guidance and orders.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -struct- 词干；近义组收其他表示「指引」与「命令」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning designed for teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「教学用的」。

entries.definition: The act of building something physical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「建造」，指实体施工。

entries.definition: The opposite of building, with de- meaning down.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「破坏」，前缀 de- 表「向下」。

entries.definition: Guidance on where to go or what to do, often spoken.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指引」，常指口头的。

entries.definition: A book of instructions for a device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「使用手册」，指设备说明书。

entries.definition: Help and advice over time, gentler than instruction.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指导」，比 instruction 温和。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the building stem and the plural habit behind most real instructions.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「建造」词干，以及真实使用中「说明」多为复数的习惯。

normal.en: struct- builds: instruction is knowledge stacked in steps.
normal.cn: struct- 建造：instruction 是分步叠起的知识。

normal.en: Instructions usually come in the plural when printed.
normal.cn: 印在纸上的说明通常用复数 instructions。

normal.en: Follow the instructions and the shelf will fit together.
normal.cn: 照着说明做，书架就能拼起来。

normal.en: Instructional materials are made for teaching.
normal.cn: instructional materials 是教学材料。

normal.en: Give clear instructions, then check they were understood.
normal.cn: 给清晰的指示，然后确认对方听懂了。

abstract.en: Picture a folded paper sliding out of a new box.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折纸从新盒子里滑出来。

abstract.en: Good instructions leave no room for guessing.
abstract.cn: 好的说明不给猜测留空间。

abstract.en: Instruction is a bridge built between two minds.
abstract.cn: instruction 是架在两个头脑之间的桥。

examples.en: Read the instructions carefully before use.
examples.cn: 使用前请仔细阅读说明。

examples.en: He gave clear instructions to the new staff.
examples.cn: 他向新员工下达了清晰的指示。

examples.en: The course offers instruction in basic statistics.
examples.cn: 这门课提供基础统计学的教学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯抓克神」——因为抓得准，才能写出神气的说明

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: written guidance, an order from authority, and teaching in general.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：书面说明、上级指示，以及泛指的教学。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded sheet slides from the box and lists the steps in order.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张折页从盒中滑出，按序列出步骤。

branches.en: THE SHEET: written steps for using something.
branches.cn: 纸张这条线：使用某物的书面步骤。

branches.en: THE RADIO: an order arriving from authority.
branches.cn: 无线电这条线：来自权力的命令。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the activity of teaching itself.
branches.cn: 学校这条线：教学这一活动本身。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are organised guidance, one on paper and one in a room.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都是有组织的指导，一在纸上，一在课堂。

branches.en: THE TONE: the order sense is the most official.
branches.cn: 语气线：「指示」义最正式。

intro.cn: instruction 是词干 instruct- 加拉丁名词词尾 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin instruere and instructio are attested; the noun of action is regular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instruere 与 instructio 均有记载，行为名词构成规则。

items.exampleCN: 它标出建造发生在内部。

definition_zh: 仪器；器械；乐器；工具；手段
definition_en: a tool or device used for a particular purpose, especially for music, measuring, or surgery
core_image: 桌面上摊开一把小提琴、一把卡尺和一支手术钳
scene: 维修台上工具按大小排开，最细的那把镊子闪着光。The clinic bought a new instrument for measuring blood pressure.
sceneCN: 这里 instrument 是「仪器、器械」（第 1 个义项：为特定用途制作的工具或装置），句意是诊所买了一台测血压的新仪器。画面里能看到的物件：镊子、卡尺、维修台。

pos.zh: 名词：仪器；器械；乐器；工具；手段

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「起重要作用的；器乐的」

由 instrumental 加 -ist 构成，义为「器乐演奏者」

senses.title: A device for a purpose
senses.definition: a tool or piece of equipment made for careful or technical work, such as measuring or surgery
senses.definitionCN: 为精细或技术性工作制作的工具或设备，如测量、手术用
senses.example: The dentist laid out her instruments in a row.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医把器械排成一排。
senses.why: Latin instruere "to equip" gives instrumentum, "that with which one is equipped".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instruere「装备」给出 instrumentum，意为「用来装备自己的东西」。

senses.title: A musical instrument
senses.definition: an object such as a violin or a flute that is played to make music
senses.definitionCN: 小提琴、长笛等用来演奏音乐的器物
senses.example: He can play three instruments but sings badly.
senses.exampleCN: 他会演奏三种乐器，但唱歌很差。
senses.why: Music moved into the same word because the body and its pipes are also equipment for an effect.
senses.whyCN: 音乐进入这个词，是因为身体与其吹管同样是产生效果的「装备」。

senses.title: A means of achieving something
senses.definition: a person, law, or method used as a way of getting something done
senses.definitionCN: 被用来促成某事的人、法律或方法
senses.example: Language is the main instrument of thought.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是思维的主要工具。
senses.why: The equipment imagery widens to anything used as a means, including laws and words.
senses.whyCN: 「装备」的意象扩大到任何被用作手段的东西，包括法律与语言。

intro.en: Instrument comes from Latin instrumentum "equipment", built on instruere "to equip, arrange".
intro.cn: instrument 来自拉丁语 instrumentum「装备、器械」，由 instruere「装备、安排」构成。

items.en: Struere "to build, pile up" is the root that also gives structure.
items.cn: struere「建造、堆积」也是 structure 的词根。

items.en: Instruere meant to equip or set out in order.
items.cn: instruere 意为「装备、按序陈设」。

items.en: Instrumentum was any equipment, a document, or a means.
items.cn: instrumentum 指任何装备、文书或手段。

items.en: Old French instrument named tools and musical instruments in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语 instrument 在中世纪指工具与乐器。

items.en: Science and medicine gave the word its precise modern sense of a measuring device.
items.cn: 科学与医学赋予它「测量装置」这一精确的现代含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -stru- building stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for tools and devices.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -stru-「建造」词干；近义组收其他表示「工具、装置」的词。

entries.definition: Playing an important part, or music without words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「起重要作用的」或「器乐的」。

entries.definition: The arrangement of parts in a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结构」。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to equip or teach.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装备；教导」。

entries.definition: The plain general word for something held and used.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工具」，最一般的说法。

entries.definition: A machine made for a specific job, often small.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「装置」，常指小型机器。

entries.definition: A set of equipment for scientific use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「仪器设备」，多指科学用成套设备。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the "equipment" sense inside the word and its three big fields.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用词内「装备」之义，以及这个词的三大领域。

normal.en: instruere is to equip: an instrument is equipment for a special job.
normal.cn: instruere 是装备：instrument 是为特定工作准备的装备。

normal.en: One word covers violins, scalpels and rulers.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖小提琴、手术刀与尺子。

normal.en: Play an instrument; use an instrument.
normal.cn: 演奏乐器用 play an instrument；使用器械用 use an instrument。

normal.en: Instrumental means playing a key part.
normal.cn: instrumental 义为「起关键作用的」。

normal.en: Same stem as instruct and structure.
normal.cn: 与 instruct、structure 同词干。

abstract.en: Picture a table where a violin, a caliper and a scalpel lie side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上小提琴、卡尺与手术刀并排放着。

abstract.en: Every instrument extends a hand.
abstract.cn: 每一件器械都是手的延伸。

abstract.en: Ideas too can be instruments, sharp or blunt.
abstract.cn: 思想也可以是工具，或利或钝。

examples.en: The laboratory instruments are checked every year.
examples.cn: 实验室仪器每年检测一次。

examples.en: The violin is the instrument she plays best.
examples.cn: 小提琴是她最擅长的乐器。

examples.en: The law was used as an instrument of change.
examples.cn: 这项法律被用作变革的工具。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬是吹门他」——他硬是吹着门上的乐器，可见是乐器

root: 拉丁语 struere「建造」→ instruere「装备、按序陈设」→ instrumentum「装备、器械、手段」→ 古法语 instrument → 中古英语。与 instruct、structure、instrumental 同族，现代科学和医学使其专指精密测量器械。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a technical device, a musical object, and a means to an end.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：专业技术器械、乐器，以及达到目的的手段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a violin, a caliper and a scalpel lie open on the same table.
core.cn: 核心意象：小提琴、卡尺与手术刀摊在同一张桌上。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: precise devices for measuring and repairing.
branches.cn: 诊所这条线：用于测量与修复的精密器械。

branches.en: THE ENSEMBLE: an object built to make music.
branches.cn: 乐队这条线：为发出音乐而造的器物。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: a law or a language treated as a tool.
branches.cn: 论证这条线：法律或语言被当作工具。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are things used to get an effect.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都是用来产生效果的东西。

branches.en: THE PLEASURE: the music sense is the warmest of the three.
branches.cn: 语气线：乐器义最富情感温度。

intro.en: Instrument is the Latin stem instru- plus the noun ending -mentum, English -ment.
intro.cn: instrument 是拉丁词干 instru- 加名词词尾 -mentum（英语 -ment）。

latinIntro.en: Latin instruere and instrumentum are well recorded, so this layer is fully attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instruere 与 instrumentum 记载充分，这一层完全有据。

definition_zh: 侮辱；辱骂；侮辱性的言行
definition_en: to say or do something rude that offends someone, or such an offensive remark
core_image: 一个人当众把对方的东西扔到地上，转头就走
scene: 饭桌上本来还有笑声，一句话出口后所有人都不说话了。He did not mean to insult her, but the joke was cruel.
sceneCN: 这里 insult 是动词「侮辱」（第 1 个义项：说或做冒犯他人的无礼之事），句意是他并不是想侮辱她，但那个玩笑很伤人。画面里能看到的物件：餐具、被扔下的东西、沉默的餐桌。

pos.zh: 名词：侮辱；侮辱性的言行

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词构成，义为「侮辱性的」
由 insulting 加 -ly 构成，义为「带侮辱地」
由过去分词构成，义为「感到受辱的」

senses.title: To speak or act rudely
senses.definition: to say or do something that shows disrespect and makes someone feel hurt or angry
senses.definitionCN: 说出或做出表示不尊重、使对方受伤或愤怒的言行
senses.example: He insulted the waiter and then left without paying.
senses.exampleCN: 他侮辱了服务员，然后没付钱就走了。
senses.why: Latin insultare means to leap upon; an insult is a verbal leap onto someone else's dignity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 insultare 意为「跳上去攻击」；侮辱是言语上跳到别人尊严上的攻击。

senses.title: A rude remark or act
senses.definition: a remark or action that is deliberately disrespectful
senses.definitionCN: 故意表示不敬的话语或举动
senses.example: Calling the work amateur was an insult to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 说这份工作是业余水平，是对整个团队的侮辱。
senses.why: The verb becomes a countable noun: each leap becomes a named thing you can take.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为可数名词：每一次「扑击」都变成一件可以「承受」的具体事。

senses.title: Something felt as disrespect
senses.definition: an event or offer that seems to show contempt, often unintentionally
senses.definitionCN: 看似表示轻蔑、往往并非有意的事件或提议
senses.example: Offering her the smaller office seemed like an insult.
senses.exampleCN: 给她那间小办公室，看来像是一种侮辱。
senses.why: The sense depends on the receiver: the same act insults one person and not another.
senses.whyCN: 这一义取决于接受方：同一行为对某些人是侮辱，对另一些人不是。

intro.en: Insult comes from Latin insultare "to leap upon", originally used of jumping on an enemy or a fallen body.
intro.cn: insult 来自拉丁语 insultare「跳上去」，最初用于跳上敌人或倒地的身体。

items.en: Salire "to leap" is the root behind assault and result as well as insult.
items.cn: salire「跳」是 assault、result 与 insult 共同的词根。

items.en: Insultare meant to leap upon, and by extension to trample or mock.
items.cn: insultare 意为「跳上去」，引申为践踏、嘲弄。

items.en: The verb was common in the Latin Bible for mocking the fallen.
items.cn: 这一动词在拉丁语圣经中常用于嘲笑倒地之人。

items.en: Old French insulter entered English with the sense of mocking words.
items.cn: 古法语 insulter 带着「言语嘲弄」义进入英语。

items.en: The noun split its pronunciation: stress on the first syllable in modern use.
items.cn: 名词与动词读音分化：现代名词重音在第一音节。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin "leap" root; the near-meaning group holds other words for offensive speech.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁「跳」词根；近义组收其他表示冒犯性言语的词。

entries.definition: A physical attack, from the same leaping root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「袭击」，词根同为「跳」。

entries.definition: Something that springs back out, literally "leaps back".
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果」，字面是「跳回去」。

entries.definition: The adjective describing rude words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「侮辱性的」。

entries.definition: To hurt someone's feelings, often without intending to.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「冒犯」，常非故意。

entries.definition: To make fun of someone in a cruel way.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「讥笑」，带有恶意。

entries.definition: To make someone feel small and ashamed in public.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使羞辱」，指当众使人羞耻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the "leap upon" image and the stress difference between verb and noun.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「跳上去」的意象，以及动名词的重音差别。

normal.en: in plus salire: to leap onto someone's dignity.
normal.cn: in 加 salire：跳到别人的尊严上。

normal.en: Verb in-SULT, noun IN-sult.
normal.cn: 动词重音在后：in-SULT；名词重音在前：IN-sult。

normal.en: Add insult to injury means heaping pain on pain.
normal.cn: add insult to injury 意为雪上加霜。

normal.en: Same root as assault and result.
normal.cn: 与 assault、result 同根。

normal.en: Take it as an insult is about the receiver, not the speaker.
normal.cn: take it as an insult 取决于听者，而非说者。

abstract.en: Picture a boot stepping on a fallen flag.
abstract.cn: 想象一只靴子踩在掉落的旗帜上。

abstract.en: An insult is a leap upward that leaves someone lower.
abstract.cn: 侮辱是一次向上的跳，却让另一个人更低。

abstract.en: The hardest insults to forgive are the ones that were true.
abstract.cn: 最难原谅的侮辱，是那些说得没错的。

examples.en: She felt deeply insulted by the question.
examples.cn: 这个问题让她深感侮辱。

examples.en: The remark was meant as a joke, not an insult.
examples.cn: 那句话本意是玩笑，不是侮辱。

examples.en: He traded insults with the referee and was sent off.
examples.cn: 他和裁判互相辱骂，被罚下场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬骚他」——硬是拿话骚他，就是侮辱

root: 拉丁语 salire「跳」→ in- + salire = insultare「跳上去攻击、践踏」→ 拉丁圣经中用于嘲弄倒地者 → 古法语 insulter → 十六世纪英语。sal- 也见于 assault、result。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the act of offending, the offensive remark itself, and something taken as contempt.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：冒犯的行为、冒犯的言辞本身，以及被视为轻蔑的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone throws an object to the ground in public and walks away.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人当众把对方的东西扔到地上，转身离开。

branches.en: THE ACT: words or actions that leap onto another person.
branches.cn: 行为这条线：跳到别人身上的言语或举动。

branches.en: THE REMARK: the single offensive sentence you can count.
branches.cn: 言语这条线：可以数出来的那一句冒犯之词。

branches.en: THE OFFER: an unintended slight that lands as contempt.
branches.cn: 提议这条线：无意之中落到对方身上像轻蔑的举动。

branches.en: THE LINK: the verb and noun name the same leap from two sides.
branches.cn: 连接线：动词与名词是同一「跃击」的两面。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: this sense lives in the ear of the receiver.
branches.cn: 镜像线：这一义存在于听者的感受里。

intro.en: Insult is in- "upon" plus the Latin leaping root sal-, with a participle stem.
intro.cn: insult 是 in-「向上、朝向」加拉丁「跳」词根 sal-，再带分词词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin salire, insultare and the noun insultus are recorded; the deeper origin of salire is not certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salire、insultare 与名词 insultus 均有记载，salire 的更早来源不确定。
